category_title: Young children with persistent challenging behaviors and communication delays
minimal_context: Kayden is at the childcare center during the routine transition to clean up toys and line up.
dialogue:
TUTOR: This is the one-minute warning signal before cleanup starts.

STUDENT: (Continues playing with the toys as the transition warning signal is given.)

TUTOR: Okay, time is up. Please clean up your toys and go line up.

STUDENT: (Drops the toys on the floor and tries to quickly walk over to line up before the other children.)

TUTOR: Kayden, you need to come back and put your toys away in the bin first.

STUDENT: (Grabs the toys, throws them across the room to get out of cleaning up, and runs back to the line.)

options.A: Adding a visual schedule to make the cleanup routine explicit, using a series of pictures showing Kayden in the toy area with lights off, putting a toy in the bin, placing the bin on the shelf, and standing on a shape in line.
options.B: Addressing Kayden's feelings mutually rather than repressing them, allowing for the exploration of his disappointments and constraints during the cleanup transition and other daily routines at the center.
options.C: Implementing genuine multicultural curricula that address race and disability, acknowledging Kayden's realities and treating him as a respected source of knowledge during center activities and daily routines.
options.D: Listening to and supporting Kayden's needs through shared power by compromising, negotiating situations, or sharing decisions, instead of trying to impose control over his behavior during the cleanup routine.
